propositions: A blocked session encountering a lock timeout sees only a bare PID of the holder, making it impossible to determine if interrupting the holder is safe or what operation holds the lock.
Compaction sweeps hold the store write lock for extended periods and are safely interruptible without data loss, but this fact is not communicated to operators via lock timeout messages.

The lock owner stamp and timeout message must label the holder as a compaction sweep using an ambient contextvar-based operation label mechanism that does not require changes to the per-ticket acquisition call site.
The LockTimeout error message must include remedial guidance stating that a compaction-sweep holder is interruptible and data-safe to terminate.
The v2 lock stamp format must remain colon-free and forward-compatible, with the operation label as an optional sanitized key=value field that staleness logic ignores.
